programme: CREB1 and ATF1, paralogous CRE/ATF-family bZIP transcription factors, both carry TGFB2 and TGFBR2 in their target sets, i.e. they transcriptionally induce the TGF-β ligand and its receptor. SMAD2, the canonical intracellular effector activated by that receptor, itself targets TGFBR2 and TGFB1 alongside matrix/EMT genes (MMP1, MMP2, SERPINE1, COL1A2, VEGFA, CCN2). The three factors therefore converge on the same axis: CRE-driven transcription of TGF-β ligand/receptor feeding SMAD2-dependent output.
role_in_a: In Huntington's disease, elevated TGF-β signalling is reported to accompany a quiescent state in the hippocampal neurogenic niche (PMID 20535034), placing the SMAD2 arm of this axis in HD tissue. Neither CREB1 nor ATF1 is directly placed in HD by any retrieved paper; their contribution here is inferred only from their shared targeting of TGFB2/TGFBR2 with SMAD2.
role_in_b: In thyroid cancer, CREB1 is reported to drive tumour progression and immune evasion (PMID 39863628) and to be a direct target of an oncogenic regulator (PMID 37529875), while SMAD2/TGF-β signalling is separately reported to drive EMT in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PMID 42301509, 40742091). ATF1 has no thyroid-specific citation in the record.
shared_axis: TGF-β/SMAD2 signalling is independently documented in each disease – restraining proliferation in the HD-relevant neurogenic niche, promoting EMT in thyroid carcinoma – and the CRE-family factors CREB1/ATF1 sit upstream of it in both tissues by virtue of transcribing the ligand/receptor genes that feed SMAD2. A pathway that is genuinely pleiotropic across growth-restraint and EMT contexts would be expected to recur in both a neurodegenerative and a proliferative tissue for this reason.
reasoning: SMAD2 is independently cited in both diseases (hippocampal TGF-β elevation in HD; TGF-β-driven EMT in PTC), and CREB1 is independently cited in thyroid cancer, so the module is nameable and partly placed by the record rather than by reasoning alone. It stays moderate rather than strong because ATF1 – one of the three carrying factors – is not placed in either disease by any retrieved paper; its role rests entirely on shared target-gene membership (TGFB2, TGFBR2) with CREB1 and SMAD2, and ReMap binding evidence for CREB1/ATF1 is thin (1 of 25 targets bound) and does not confirm occupancy at TGFB2/TGFBR2 specifically.
support: PMID 20535034 – elevated TGF-β associated with hippocampal neurogenic-niche stem cell quiescence, an HD model context. PMID 42301509 – GOLPH3 promotes papillary thyroid carcinoma via the TGF-β pathway. PMID 40742091 – ASAP1 promotes EMT by activating TGFβ signalling in papillary thyroid carcinoma. PMID 39863628 – exosomal CREB1 promotes thyroid cancer progression and immune evasion. PMID 37529875 – MEX3A induces thyroid cancer development via targeting CREB1.
how_to_falsify: In a thyroid cancer line, co-deplete CREB1 and ATF1 and measure TGFB2/TGFBR2 transcript levels and downstream SMAD2 phosphorylation/nuclear translocation; if TGFB2/TGFBR2 expression and SMAD2 activation are unaffected, the proposed CRE-family → TGF-β induction link fails. Separately, ChIP for CREB1/ATF1 occupancy at the TGFB2 and TGFBR2 loci in an HD-relevant hippocampal or striatal model – absence of binding would refute the module in the tissue where the HD evidence (PMID 20535034) actually sits.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (HD network) versus thyroid tumour tissue; the one piece of HD-side evidence for this axis (PMID 20535034) concerns a hippocampal neurogenic niche, not blood, so translating the blood-derived network signal to that mechanism is an extra inferential step. Of 483 patient-group comparisons only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie them, so the apparent robustness (188/483, 174/483, 155/483) reflects mostly within-cohort replication rather than broad independent confirmation. CREB5, a close CREB-family paralog, was removed as tissue-generic in this pairing – a reminder that CRE-binding activity broadly is common in these tissues, and CREB1/ATF1 stand out only by their specific concordance pattern, not because CRE-family binding itself is rare here. ReMap binding is sparse (1/25 targets for both CREB1 and ATF1) and does not confirm binding at TGFB2/TGFBR2 specifically. HEY2, independently linked to thyroid cancer via Notch/Wnt signalling (PMID 41303715, 37051101, 31565805), was considered but excluded from the programme because it has no Huntington's-disease-side evidence (no Open Targets association, no citation), so it does not support a shared axis on the terms this task requires.
